question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, CIO of Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III AIF), is explaining the 'principle of pooling' to a new analyst. Which of the following BEST captures the essence of pooling as applied to a Cat III AIF?

answer.text: Each investor's corpus is managed in a ring-fenced sub-account under a discretionary PMS agreement with the manager
Contributions from investors are combined into a common blind-pool corpus that the manager deploys under a single investment strategy
Investors co-invest directly into each investee security in their name, with the manager providing only trade-execution support
Every investor receives an individual demat account, with the manager only recommending trades on a non-discretionary basis

explanation.text: The Logic: Pooling means contributions from multiple investors are combined into a single common corpus, which the manager deploys under one investment strategy — a 'blind pool'. This is distinct from portfolio management services, where each investor's corpus is kept distinct and managed separately. Pooling allows the manager to run one strategy at scale on behalf of all investors. The Trap: Options A and D describe a portfolio management services arrangement, not an AIF. Option C describes direct investment / advisory, not pooling. Only Option B captures the AIF blind-pool concept. Note: The principle of pooling and the blind-pool concept are explained in the workbook on pp. 118-119.
